title: Private inbox
description: Messaging inside an organization: send, list, mark read, delete from your own view and block senders, with a noninterference theorem saying what each user may learn.
author: Claude (agent-authored explanation; review before relying on it)
exclusions: Timing, latency and SERIALIZABLE retries are channels outside the kernel's result; noninterference does not cover them.
Noninterference is about one command at a time. What a user infers from watching their view change over many steps, for example Bob's mark_read changing Alice's sent box, is outside it.
The view grants whole message rows, so the theorem allows a sender to learn whether the recipient deleted a message; the JSON happens not to print it.
Authentication, the JSON codec, HTTP status mapping and reply rendering are trusted shell code.
Isolation between organizations is a framework property, not part of these theorems.
Acceptance of valid messages, deletes and reads is shown on concrete scenarios, not proven for every state.
Migrated or externally modified rows are not automatically in the modeled reachable set.

nodes.title: Nothing about other people's mail reaches you
nodes.description: Whatever you do, the reply, the error code and the writes depend only on the messages you sent or received and on who has blocked you. Messages between other people and other people's blocks cannot change your outcome.
excludes: Covers the kernel's result only, not how long it takes: the engine loads the whole organization and the kernel scans every message, so latency and SERIALIZABLE retries depend on other people's traffic.

nodes.title: Other people's conversations cannot be probed
nodes.description: A message between two other users gets exactly the same answer as one that was never sent, so you cannot learn that a conversation exists or how long it is by trying keys.
excludes: Timing is not covered: the kernel scans every message, so a probe's latency can still depend on other people's conversations.

nodes.title: You learn whether someone blocked you, and nothing more
nodes.description: A refused send tells you that the recipient blocked you. This is the one fact about blocks in your view: you cannot learn whom else the recipient blocked, nor anything about other people's blocks.

nodes.title: Listings show only your own messages
nodes.description: Every message in an inbox or sent listing was sent or received by the caller.

nodes.title: Your commands never change other people's rows
nodes.description: A successful command writes only messages you sent or received and blocks you own. Afterwards, every message not involving you and every block owned by someone else is exactly as it was.

nodes.title: Sending never overwrites a message
nodes.description: A new message gets a key (sender, recipient, number) that no existing message has, with a number above every earlier one in that conversation.

nodes.title: Messages only move forward
nodes.description: No command changes a message's text or clears its read or deleted flags. A message deleted from someone's view never comes back for them.

nodes.title: A blocked sender cannot deliver
nodes.description: A send succeeds only when the recipient has not blocked the sender. The block applies only to that pair: the blocked user can still write to everyone else.

nodes.title: Keys stay unique and texts stay valid
nodes.description: In every state reachable from an empty inbox, message keys and block keys are unique and every stored text is 1 to 1000 bytes.

nodes.title: The database keeps the invariants
nodes.description: Accepted write sets committed to PostgreSQL, interleaved with other tenants' commits, leave rows whose state satisfies the invariants, and every later load decodes to such a state.

nodes.title: Committing does what the specification says
nodes.description: Applying a write set in the kernel computes the specified state change, and the store holds the encoding of that state with loads decoding back to it up to row order.

nodes.title: No command crashes the kernel
nodes.description: Every command on every snapshot returns a result: the kernel never panics, overflows arithmetic or indexes out of bounds.

nodes.title: Messages are delivered and numbered
nodes.description: A valid message to someone who has not blocked you is accepted and appears in their inbox; the first message of a conversation is number 0. Shown on concrete runs, not for every state.

nodes.title: Deleting hides a message only from your side
nodes.description: A participant can delete a message from their own view; the other side keeps their copy and its flags. A non-participant cannot delete it.

nodes.title: Only the recipient marks a message read
nodes.description: A successful mark_read writes a message the caller received and has not deleted, changing only its read flag.

nodes.title: Noninterference
nodes.description: For any principal a, snapshots s1 and s2 and command c: if view(s1, a.user) = view(s2, a.user), then transition a s1 c = transition a s2 c, the whole result including writes, reply and error.

nodes.title: Block lookup is in the view
nodes.description: With equal views for u, whether d blocks u gives the same answer in both snapshots. This is the lemma that uses the block part of the view.

nodes.title: Lookups naming the caller agree
nodes.description: With equal views for u, looking up a message whose sender or recipient is u gives the same answer in both snapshots.

nodes.title: Conversation numbering agrees
nodes.description: With equal views for u, the largest number from u to d is the same in both snapshots, so the next number reveals nothing beyond the conversation.

nodes.title: Listings agree
nodes.description: With equal views for u, the inbox and sent listings of u are the same in both snapshots.

nodes.title: Replies are confined
nodes.description: If a command succeeds with a Messages reply, every message in it involves the caller.

nodes.title: Writes are confined
nodes.description: If a command succeeds, every write it returns touches only the caller's rows: a message involving the caller, or a block the caller owns.

nodes.title: Others' rows unchanged
nodes.description: If a command succeeds, applying its writes leaves others(s, caller), the messages not involving the caller and blocks owned by someone else, equal to what it was. No invariant is assumed.

nodes.title: Six kinds of success
nodes.description: Sums up the command lemmas: a successful command is a listing with no writes, a send of a fresh message, a mark_read, a delete on the caller's side, a block or an unblock of the caller's own block.

nodes.title: Transition is total
nodes.description: For every principal, snapshot and command there is some r with transition a s c = ok r: the extracted code never fails.

nodes.title: Fresh message key
nodes.description: If a send succeeds, it writes exactly one message m and no message in the current state has msgKey equal to msgKey m.

nodes.title: Messages kept
nodes.description: For a Reachable state and a successful command, every message after the step with the key of a message before it is Later than it: same text, flags only turn on.

nodes.title: Invariant preserved
nodes.description: If Inv holds before a successful command, it holds after applying the command's writes.

nodes.title: Invariant on reachable states
nodes.description: Every Reachable state satisfies Inv.

nodes.title: What send does
nodes.description: If send succeeds, the text is valid, the recipient has no block against the sender, and it writes one new message with a number above every earlier one from sender to recipient, replying with that number.

nodes.title: What mark_read does
nodes.description: If mark_read succeeds, it found a message addressed to the caller that the caller has not deleted, and writes it back with read set.

nodes.title: What delete does
nodes.description: If delete succeeds, the key names the caller as sender or recipient, the message exists, and the single write is that message hidden on the caller's side (hideFor).

nodes.title: Numbering bound
nodes.description: Every message from f to t has a number below rank(lastSeq ms f t), which is what makes the next number fresh.

nodes.title: apply computes applyAll
nodes.description: If total rows plus writes stay below Usize.max, the kernel's apply returns a snapshot whose list form equals applyAll of the write set.

nodes.title: Store holds the applied state
nodes.description: For a Served database, the tables hold enc of the state, and decoding a full load yields a snapshot equivalent to it up to row order.

nodes.title: Invariant on the database
nodes.description: For a valid two-table schema and an integer tenant, every PgServed database built from Accepted write sets holds a state satisfying Inv, and every later load decodes to a snapshot satisfying Inv.

nodes.title: Scenario: Alice sends
nodes.description: On an empty snapshot, Alice's send of "hi" to Bob succeeds with one PutMessage and reply Sent 0.

nodes.title: Scenario: Bob reads
nodes.description: After Alice's message, Bob's inbox listing is exactly that message.

nodes.title: Scenario: Carol sees nothing
nodes.description: In the same state, Carol's inbox listing is empty.

nodes.title: Scenario: Carol cannot delete
nodes.description: Carol's delete of Alice's message to Bob returns NotFound, the same error as a missing message.

nodes.title: Scenario: Bob deletes his copy
nodes.description: Bob's delete writes the message back with only recipient_deleted set, so Alice's side is untouched.

nodes.title: Scenario: block refuses
nodes.description: When Bob blocks Alice, her send to Bob returns the Blocked error.

nodes.title: Scenario: block is narrow
nodes.description: In the same state, Alice's send to Carol succeeds with number 0.

nodes.title: Scenario: Carol cannot tell
nodes.description: The empty snapshot and the one with Alice's message to Bob differ, yet every command by Carol has the same result in both. This shows noninterference is not vacuous.

nodes.title: Without blocks in the view, send would leak
nodes.description: Alice's view differs between the empty snapshot and one where Bob blocks her, and her send to Bob gets different results. If the block part were dropped from view, these two states would look the same to her, so noninterference would be false.

nodes.title: What a user may learn
nodes.description: view s u is the messages u sent or received, whole, together with the blocks naming u as sender. It excludes other people's messages and the blocks u owns.

nodes.title: Involvement
nodes.description: involves u m holds when u is the sender or the recipient of m.

nodes.title: Rows that are not yours
nodes.description: others s u is the messages not involving u and the blocks not owned by u.

nodes.title: Rows a write touches
nodes.description: A PutMessage touches u when the message involves u; PutBlock and DelBlock touch u when u owns the block.

nodes.title: Meaning of a write set
nodes.description: applyAll folds applyWrite over the writes: upsert by key for messages and blocks, filter by key for DelBlock.

nodes.title: Message key
nodes.description: A message is keyed by (sender, recipient, seq), so an upsert can only replace a message between the same two users.

nodes.title: Inbox invariant
nodes.description: Message keys are unique, every text satisfies textOk, and block keys are unique.

nodes.title: Valid text
nodes.description: A text is nonempty and at most 1000 bytes.

nodes.title: Later version of a message
nodes.description: Later m m' means the same text, and the read, sender_deleted and recipient_deleted flags only go from false to true.

nodes.title: Hiding on one side
nodes.description: hideFor u f t m sets sender_deleted when u is the sender and recipient_deleted when u is the recipient, leaving the other flag as it was.

nodes.title: What a listing keeps
nodes.description: The inbox keeps messages addressed to u that u has not deleted; the sent box keeps messages from u that u has not deleted.

nodes.title: Row encoding
nodes.description: enc maps the state to table 0 (messages) and table 1 (blocks); sqlA gives the table write for each kernel write.

nodes.title: Equal views
nodes.description: Noninterference compares two snapshots only under the hypothesis that the caller's view is equal in both. It says nothing about states whose views differ.

nodes.title: Reachable state
nodes.description: The state comes from the empty inbox by successful commands. Externally modified or migrated rows are not automatically reachable.

nodes.title: Invariant before the step
nodes.description: inv_preserved takes Inv of the starting state as a hypothesis; reachable_inv discharges it for reachable states.

nodes.title: Only successful commands
nodes.description: The one-run theorems assume transition returned Ok with a write set. A refusal commits nothing in the engine, which is part of the trusted engine contract, not of these theorems.

nodes.title: Snapshot size bound
nodes.description: apply_spec requires total rows plus the number of writes to stay below Usize.max.

nodes.title: Accepted write sets
nodes.description: db_inv covers databases built only from write sets the kernel returned for some accepted command, plus valid schema, an integer tenant column and the two tables.

nodes.title: Authenticated caller
nodes.description: The principal comes from an HMAC bearer token of the form v1.org.user.expiry.mac. The theorems hold for whatever principal is passed; secrecy of H5I_APP_SECRET and the expiry clock are trusted.

nodes.title: JSON shell
nodes.description: Decoding the command and rendering the reply and error are outside the theorem. The reply renderer prints from, to, seq, text and read, but not the deleted flags; errors become HTTP status codes as a function of the error.

nodes.title: Engine and PostgreSQL contract
nodes.description: One attempt loads one tenant, runs transition, writes and commits in a SERIALIZABLE transaction; a refusal rolls back. PostgreSQL is assumed to run the rendered SQL as modeled.

nodes.title: Stored replies for retries
nodes.description: With an Idempotency-Key, a repeat gets the stored reply. Replies are stored per tenant and per user scope u<user>, so the trusted ReplyCodec scope keeps one user's stored listing from another.

nodes.title: Tenant isolation
nodes.description: The kernel sees one organization; the framework maps the principal's org to the tenant and filters every statement by it. Isolation between organizations is a framework property, not part of these theorems.

nodes.title: Extraction fidelity
nodes.description: Theorems are about the Lean translation of the Rust produced by Charon and Aeneas, starting from transition. Re-extract after changing the kernel; the check alone does not establish freshness.

nodes.title: Deployment
nodes.description: The engine role must not be a superuser and no other service may hold its credentials; otherwise rows can change outside the kernel.

nodes.title: Store conformance tested
nodes.description: server/tests/postgres.rs runs random command sequences through PostgreSQL and the in-memory reference and checks they agree. This is a test, not a proof of PostgreSQL behavior.

nodes.title: transition
nodes.description: Dispatches Send, Inbox, Sent, MarkRead, Delete, Block and Unblock on the caller's user id, returning writes and a reply or a refusal that commits nothing.

nodes.title: send
nodes.description: Checks the text, refuses with Blocked if the recipient blocked the caller, then numbers the message one above the conversation's last number, refusing on overflow.

nodes.title: mark_read
nodes.description: Looks up the message from `from` to the caller and sets read, or answers NotFound when it is missing or deleted on the recipient's side.

nodes.title: delete
nodes.description: Refuses with NotFound before any lookup when the key does not name the caller, then hides the message on the caller's side. The declared mutant read_others_messages removes this first check.

nodes.title: mailbox
nodes.description: Filters the messages the caller received (inbox) or sent (sent box), skipping those the caller deleted.

nodes.title: Block and Unblock
nodes.description: Write or delete the block row owned by the caller.

nodes.title: Lookup helpers
nodes.description: is_blocked, last_seq, find_message and text_ok: linear scans over the loaded lists.

nodes.title: Tables and apply
nodes.description: schema! declares the messages and blocks tables with their keys and generates apply; apply_write and sql_write map each kernel write to a row change.

nodes.title: InboxStore
nodes.description: Loads both tables for a tenant with the generated schema loader and stores a write set with the generated compiled writes.

nodes.title: Kernel for Inbox
nodes.description: Connects the framework to the kernel: the tenant is the principal's org, and transition and apply call the extracted functions.

nodes.title: JSON API
nodes.description: decode_command parses the tagged JSON command with deny_unknown_fields; encode_reply and encode_error render the result.

nodes.title: POST /rpc
nodes.description: rpc_router mounts POST /rpc; the handler takes the authenticated Actor, decodes the body and calls respond, which runs the engine and renders the outcome.

nodes.title: Engine execute
nodes.description: Runs one command for the actor's tenant: load, transition, store, commit, with retries and optional idempotency.
